recipes.name: Dijonnaise Chicken
ingredients_raw: 0.25 cup prepared Dijon mustard mayonnaise blend

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Place chicken in a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Mix mustard-mayonnaise blend, olive oil, lemon juice, lemon pepper, salt, and bouillon in a bowl; pour over chicken in the baking dish.

Bake in the preheated oven until chicken is no longer pink and juices run clear, about 30 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read at least 165 degrees F (74 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Dijonnaise Chicken
raw_recipe.description: This baked chicken Dijonnaise has a great mustard taste and can be baked alone or in a casserole dish with prepared wild rice.

review.reviewBody:
I mixed a couple of teaspoons of light mayo in with the Dijonnaise (to cut the mustard flavor for my kids), used plain black pepper (all I had) and reduced the oil (only had a couple of teaspoons left in the bottle). This was SHOCKINGLY good. I am a notorious chicken over-cooker, and the texture of this ended up like an excellent rotisserie chicken. Flavor was great, a really unexpected "zesty" balance of the mustard and lemon. Couldn't be easier either! Served it with a prewashed, bagged salad and store-bought crusty whole grain bread. Everyone loved it!
My husband, kids, and I say THANK YOU TERI for taking the time to submit this recipe.

This turned out pretty well. I omitted the salt, since the sauce already included chicken bouillon granules, so that was enough sodium. Mixed up the sauce (which we really liked) in the morning and into the fridge. An easy, tasty dinner which I would make again.

I will make it again. I love a dijonnaise chicken. I have a friend, recently diabetic, & one day he might even visit, but I'm trying to make recipes that are less fatty, flavourful & relatively simple & this is! The addition of lemon is perfect for a warm winter in Australia with salad through the year. We accompanied it with rye bread so all the saucy goodness isn't wasted & helps fill hungry kids ensuring it lasts longer. For diabetics I'm using plain mustard including mustard seeds & grilling it to ensure I can reduce the amount of butter & have the chicken lightly browned & crispy before finishing it as a baked meal in a medium oven, but not fan-forced. It's a good base for people just starting to cook. Having less ingredients is encouraging for any new chef (son: I'm looking at you!). Simple is often best, & not just for saving time. Thank you.
Made it twice, turned out perfect. Only used 1/8 cup of olive oil, used regular pepper not lemon pepper, added rosemary, used honey Dijon mustard, omitted the bouillon cube.

Wonderful Chicken dish with a great creamy sauce. I love mustard so I used more of it than probably needed. As well, I substituted the chicken bouillon with a half teaspoon of curry and served it with rice pilaf. It turned out delicious!

I followed this recipe, but used bone in chicken breast and baked for an hour. I also made my own dijonnaise, more dijon than mayo. Also just used fresh ground pepper instead of lemon pepper. I agree about cutting back on the olive oil. This was delicious and we'll have it again.

This chicken is amazing! Zesty and flavorful. I read the reviews and made some changes. I reduced the olive oil to 2 TBSP and substituted the chicken bouillon for italian seasoning and it turned out delicious! Thanks for sharing a great recipe!

I followed the advice of several other reviewers and omitted the salt and cut the olive oil in half. Also, I mixed dijon mustard with light mayonaise in a 50-50 mixture to create dijonaise. This was absolutely outstanding!

Couldn't be easier and has a fantastic flavor. I made my own dijonnaise with a very scant 1/4 cup mayo and filled the rest of the measuring cup with dijon. Gave a nice strong mustard flavor. Will definitely be making again. Tastes like you put a lot more work into it for sure!

I love this recipe!! I haven't made chicken any other way since I found this. I did cut down on the oil and left the bullion out. And I used dijon mustard and light mayo rather than the prepared blend that you can buy already made up. but this is yummy

I changed it a bit for what I had on hand and it was wonderful! Seasoned the chicken breasts well with garlic, salt, pepper and a dash of cayenne... Browned them quickly in the olive oil. I substituted worcershire sauce for the lemon wich gave it some zing. Then I baked with the Dijonnaise sauce without the oil. Good!

I feel really terrible saying it, because I really appreciate that someone took the time and care to contribute this recipe, but it was disgusting. :( I made it as written. The texture of the chicken was good, but I did not like the flavor. I had to wash the sauce off and eat the chicken plain. If you love lemon pepper, maybe your experience will differ. It was not for me, sadly.
this was delicious! We love dijon mustard and this was a real treat. I didn't have breasts so l used thighs instead so I know it will really be good using them. I will be using this often.
Delicious, however I would cut out the salt altogether next time.
We liked this recipe. I did it exactly as written. I will definitely make it again. I have other recipes that we like a little better.

Yummy! A little salty but I like that. If you don't I would reduce the salt some. I might add a little more oil next time because my son didn't care for how thick the sauce was on top of the chicken. All in all easy and tasty!
Nice and easy to prep the night before
Great flavor!
Yummy......used 1/2 mayo & 1/2 Dijon. Only 2 T oil and no bouillon
needed a bit of honey
